chunks: My father (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa narrated to me, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Malik ibn 'Atiyya, from Abu Hamza, from Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir (peace be upon him).

He said: I heard him say: Indeed, no year has less rain than another; rather, God places it wherever He wills. When a people commit sins, God, exalted is His majesty, diverts from them what He had apportioned for them of rain in that year to others, and to the deserts, the seas, and the mountains. Indeed, God even punishes the scarab beetle in its burrow by withholding rain from the land where it dwells, because of the sins of those in its vicinity, though God has given it a passage to a path away from the locality of the sinful people.
Then Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: So take heed, O people of insight.

Then he said: We found in the Book of Ali (peace be upon him), he said: The Messenger of God (may God's blessings be upon him and his family) said: When fornication becomes prevalent, sudden deaths increase. When the measure is cheated, God seizes them with years of famine and shortage. When they withhold the almsgiving (zakat), the earth is prevented from its blessings of crops, fruits, and all its minerals. When they are unjust in their rulings, they cooperate in oppression and aggression. When they break their covenants, God empowers their enemy over them. When they sever family ties, wealth is placed in the hands of the wicked. And when they do not enjoin good, do not forbid evil, and do not follow the chosen ones from my Ahl al-Bayt, God empowers the worst among them over them, and then the best among them supplicate but are not answered.

key_terms.أهل بيتي: Ahl al-Bayt, the Prophet's household, whose guidance is essential
key_terms.الأمر بالمعروف والنهي عن المنكر: Enjoining good and forbidding evil, a fundamental Islamic obligation
key_terms.الجعل: Scarab beetle (dung beetle), used as an example of innocent creatures suffering from human sins
key_terms.المعاصي: Sins, acts of disobedience against God

ai.seo_question: What are the consequences of communal sins according to Islam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (AS) teaches that rain is distributed by divine will according to the moral state of communities, not by natural variation alone -- sinful peoples have their share of rain redirected to deserts, seas, and mountains, with even insects suffering as collateral. He then cites from the Book of Imam Ali (AS) a prophetic hadith enumerating seven communal sins and their corresponding divine punishments, culminating in the warning that abandoning the Ahl al-Bayt leads to domination by the wicked and unanswered prayers.
